After 34 years in United ISD classrooms and offices, Selina Gomez came home to a Laredo campus with a new way of reaching students: as a published author.

Gomez, who spent 10 years as an assistant principal at the Alexander High School ninth grade campus, returned to its library this week to share her first book, From Gloves to Gavel, with students during the library’s October TeenTober activities, according to United ISD.

The biography honors her late father, Santiago “Jimmy” Sandoval, a Laredo native raised in the El Cuatro neighborhood whose journey took him from the boxing ring to the courtroom. Sandoval became a Golden Gloves champion in the bantamweight and featherweight divisions, boxed for seven years — including a professional run — and fought his last bout in 1967 before education opened a new chapter: he became an attorney.

“It’s so good to be home,” Gomez told the students, according to the district. Her message to them: education matters, beginnings don’t define ambitions — and never stop fighting.

“I think a true champion is a person who continues to fight in their lives,” she said. Her father’s creed, she added, was simple: “You always move forward. You never quit, you never give up. You always keep fighting.”

The book began two years ago as a remembrance card after Sandoval’s death and grew into a story about facing hardship and moving forward. Gomez spent about two years writing it and self-published through Amazon in late August, navigating formatting and publishing requirements she described as among the hardest parts of the process.

“To him, education was everything,” Gomez said of her father. “From a boxer, he became a lawyer.” That belief shaped her own career as a social studies teacher and administrator — and, she said, the two children she raised, who are pursuing college studies in radiation therapy and biomedical science.

Librarian Jessica Morales, who hosted the event at Alexander’s ninth grade and main campuses, said the goal is to expose students to authors and literacy: to “promote reading, a love of reading, and a lifelong love of learning.” Sandoval’s roots in a Laredo neighborhood, she added, bring the message of perseverance close to home for students who may doubt whether their dreams are possible because of where they come from.

From Gloves to Gavel is available for purchase through Amazon.

Sources: United Independent School District, Oct. 21, 2026.

title: From gloves to gavel: retired UISD educator honors her boxer-turned-attorney father in new book
